title: Time by the railway
text: Before the railways, every town kept its own sun. Noon in Bristol arrived a quarter of an hour after noon in London, and nobody minded: time was local, {{1}} by sundials and habit. The railways destroyed that comfort. Trains running on a timetable could not {{2}} eleven different noons between London and Edinburgh, so the companies adopted London time, and station clocks became the {{3}} to which the whole country gradually set itself. The change met surprising {{4}} from some quarters: Bristol kept local time on its cathedral clock until 1852, fitting two minute hands to the same dial, and some towns argued that railway time was an {{5}} on local liberty. Resistance proved {{6}}: legislation made Greenwich time the legal standard for all of Britain in 1880, and the world followed slowly, agreeing in 1884 on a system of global time zones {{7}} on Greenwich. The railway clock quietly rewired society: punctuality became a virtue, lateness an offence {{8}} in minutes, and 'keeping time' a national habit. The sundial survives in gardens, politely inaccurate, a souvenir of an unhurried age.

gaps.explanation: 'time was local, measured by sundials' — determined with them; mend = repair, mingle = mix socially.
'could not tolerate eleven different noons' — could not work with them; the other verbs do not mean 'accept and manage'.
'station clocks became the standard' — the reference everyone followed; statute = a law, status = social standing.
'met surprising opposition from some quarters' — resistance; obligation = duty, observation = watching or a remark.
'an infringement on local liberty' — a violation of it; indulgence = a treat, injunction = a court order.
'Resistance proved futile' — achieved nothing; fertile = productive, feigned = pretended, famed = famous.
'time zones based on Greenwich' — fixed with reference to it; 'biased on' is a classic wrong pattern (biased against/towards).
'an offence counted in minutes' — reckoned by them; recount = tell again or count again, surmount = overcome.
